The nearest distances are 1.16 / 1.70 / 2.10 / 2.25 / 1.86 / 1.42 / 1.00 b at ticks 84 / 86 / 88 / 90 / 92 / 94 / 96, against 0.08-0.39 b at 74-82. findings.title: The lock is re-asserted only once per tick, before the game's own un-spectate: while Shift is held (or after a left click on her body) the client never shows the stand's view
findings.where: data/rlk/function/mboss/cam/hold.mcfunction:15-16 (from tools/build_mboss_core.py:3387-3423); the claim in README 홍련 「조작 잠금 FN-cam」 and hr2_progress 'Only a person in the game' item 4; tools/dev/sim/hr/tests/test_cam.py:417-428 (K4)
findings.what: rlk:tick re-issues `spectate <stand>` in the command-function phase. The same tick, ServerPlayer.tick runs later in the level phase, sees the held Shift (wantsToStopRiding) and calls setCamera(this), which sends SetCamera(self) and a teleport. The client receives both in one flush, so every tick ends with the player as their own camera. For as long as Shift is held, the view is the player's free spectator view at the stand's spot (eye 0.1 b above it, scale 0.0625), snapped back 20 times a second. Between snaps the mouse turns it and Shift sinks it by up to about 0.15 b per tick, and the stand's smooth glide and pans are lost. This applies in every locked span. Inside the skip windows it lasts the 20 t a skip needs (accepted as a flicker by the brief). In the repels, the ending, the coda, and CS0/CS1 outside 20-1270 / 40-560 there is no skip, but a player who holds Shift to try one gets this view for as long as they hold it. A related case is a left click while the crosshair is on a pickable entity within reach: her husk in the close-ups, or the avatar's click shield. 26.3's handleSpectatorAction then calls setCamera(entity) between ticks, so the view jumps to that entity's eyes for about one tick until the next hold. In neither case can the player act (handleAttack returns early for spectators, and use / swap are not sent in spectator mode). The README's statement 'held during a cutscene the view should stay on the stand' is not what happens.
findings.evidence: (1) javap of the 26.3 server jar: MinecraftServer.tickChildren runs ServerFunctionManager.tick before ServerLevel.tick and the connection tick. ServerPlayer.tick, with the camera alive, calls absSnapTo, then wantsToStopRiding, then setCamera(this). ServerPlayer.setCamera sends ClientboundSetCameraPacket and teleports only when the camera changes. handleSpectatorAction calls setCamera(target) for a pickable entity within interaction range + 3 b. (2) The lane's own model agrees: test_cam K4 asserts `s.st(pl)['cam'] is None` after every tick while sneaking ('the game drops the camera after every tick'). It only checks that the hold tag and the game mode stay.
findings.repro: cd <sim copy>/hr/tests && python3 test_cam.py <roguelike> stand (K4 prints the per-tick camera: None while sneaking). In game: hold Shift through the repel or the ending, and left-click while I5 / S10 / E17 frame her face.
findings.fix: No datapack hook runs after the player tick, so this cannot be fully prevented. Correct the README and hr2 text, and keep it in the in-game list. To soften it while Shift is held: in hold, when rlk:in_sneak is true, also `tp @s` to the live stand's eye with the stand's rotation each tick, so the snapped view matches the shot. Optionally shorten the Shift-to-skip hold.

findings.title: Each locked sequence's new camera stands are summoned at the stage marker with yaw 0 and moved to the first eye in the same tick, so the client glides and spins the first shot in over 3 ticks; nothing masks it in CS0
findings.where: tools/mboss_scarlet/seq.py:652, 768, 934, 1076, 1164 (`cam/kill` + `execute at STAGE run cam/spawn`, then tick 0's shot placed in the same tick: tools/mboss_scarlet/cam.py:186-191, 'a new entity does not glide'); data/rlk/function/mboss/cam/spawn.mcfunction
findings.what: The server sends a new entity's spawn packet at summon time, with the summon position and the summon yaw: the floor at the stage origin, yaw 0. The same-tick `tp … facing` then reaches the client as a move, and the client interpolates it over 3 ticks; the lane's PRE logic depends on exactly this. CS0: the player is first held at tick 1, so the client watches the last 2 ticks of A's glide. It travels from the floor at P0 to I1's eye 7.4 b back and 1.9 b up, with a yaw swing of about 170° (0 → about 187.5°). The 1-s arrival blindness does not hide it: it is a mob effect on the player, and while spectating, the client draws fog for the camera entity, the stand. CS1: the white mask (0/2/2) is already fading while the glide finishes, and S1 lasts only 6 t. Ending tick 0 (new stands even after the repel): the white mask (0/2/1) likewise. The repel's gold mask (0/4/3) hides it. camsim models a new stand as appearing at its placed pose, so test_seq and test_cam cannot see this.
findings.evidence: (1) javap: ChunkMap.addEntity → TrackedEntity.updatePlayers → ServerEntity.addPairing → connection.send(bundle), at summon time. (2) Real 26.3 server (console probe on a copy of mcsrv): `execute positioned 3.5 120 3.5 rotated 90 0 run function rlk:mboss/cam/spawn` gives stands with Rotation [0f, 0f] at the execution position. (3) test_seq: 'the player held from tick 1' for CS0. (4) cam.py's own doc: a stand that is moved glides over 3 ticks.
findings.repro: Real server: in a server copy, `execute positioned 3.5 120 3.5 rotated 90 0 run function rlk:mboss/cam/spawn`, then `data get entity @e[tag=rlk_mb_cam2,limit=1] Rotation`, which gives [0.0f, 0.0f]. Then read seq/intro/start.mcfunction (spawn at the stage, then lock → cam → c/0 places I1 in the same tick).
findings.fix: Summon the stands at the first shot's eye with its rotation in the NBT. For example, a macro `cam/spawn_at {yaw,pitch}` run `positioned <eye>` with Rotation:[$(yaw)f,$(pitch)f], or summon them one tick (better PRE ticks) before the lock starts. Alternatively, keep the stands across sequences and give tick 0's shot the same PRE placement as every other cut. Then model the spawn packet in camsim.

findings.title: E2 ends on an empty frame for 10 ticks (ending 84-93): both figures are shoved out of a static shot before the cut

findings.what: The shove (80-90) moves her to f 6.0 and the actor to f -0.6. From 84, her head, her pelvis and the actor's head are all outside the 16:9 frame at 70° (61° and 75° off the view axis) until the cut at 94, so the shot shows only sky and grass for half a second. findings.evidence: A per-tick frustum check of the built track (cam.Track via seq.tracks()) against her_tracks.json and the actor manifest finds this as the only unintended empty span among the 4 sequences; the empty spans I14 and S5 are intended. A render with her real rig and the real actor at ending 93 is empty.
findings.repro: For t in 80..94: built camera = seq.tracks()['ending'].shot_at(t).at(t). Project her_tracks clips.ending head/pelvis[t] and the manifest's clips.ending.tick.head[t] into a 70° vertical, 16:9 frame: nothing is inside from 84 to 93.
findings.fix: Cut to E3 at about 84, or pull B back / pan with the shove over 80-90 (for example to ST(4.5, 1.8, 2.2) looking at ST(0, 1.3, 2.7)), or start E3 on the actor's skid at 84.

Server jar (javap): spectate refuses non-spectators and only types with clientTrackingRange 0. setCamera does nothing for the same entity (the per-tick spectate sends nothing). handleAttack returns early for spectators, so a held player cannot hit anything (no attack, no interaction-entity click). A spectator's use/swap are not sent.

FN-cam wiring: rlk:tick holds and releases right after mboss/main; the two-player guard releases before stripping tags. mboss/main, cleanup_fight and init zero the request; cleanup_fight, init and uninstall release; view/tick rests behind its guard; lvup/tick ignores a held player's sneak tap. Developer mode is never locked. A request without a live fight, an avatar or the live stand releases at once.
A held player cannot open the map or the selection space (G menu / Shift+F): both refuse while #combat room ≥ 1, which the rift's room/combat_start sets for the special fight.

Relog traced through the code. On a server: the fight pauses (no tagged player), the release runs on the first tick back, and the player goes to the stored camret (the avatar was swept). In single player: view/fresh → teardown, then release → camret, then the avatar is rebuilt the next tick. Game mode comes from the hold tags in both cases.

The release restores the game mode, un-spectates, moves the player to the avatar (or camret) facing her, re-seats unless sneaking, stops the actor and shows the avatar (main hand back from hotbar.0). The avatar never holds an off-hand item, so hide's off-hand clear loses nothing.
